sections.heading: How to Play Fury Warrior
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Fury Warrior"][color=warrior]Fury Warrior Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
[tr][td]
Fury Warriors revolve around maximizing [spell=184361] uptime and dealing damage through fast-paced attacks and a variety of special abilities, excelling at dealing high multitarget damage while sacrificing little to no single target to do so.

[hr]
[table]
[tr]
[td width=7%][icon name=ability_warrior_charge size=medium type=round color=c1 inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b][color=warrior]Avoid Downtime[/color][/b] - Fury generates the majority of its rage from abilities, so reducing the amount of time spent chasing, running out mechanics, or otherwise not hitting the boss is critical to maximizing performance. There are several abilities to help with this, such as [spell=100] and [spell=6544], so use them smartly to stay on target as much as possible![/td]
[/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
[tr]
[td width=7%][icon name=ability_warrior_innerrage size=medium type=round color=c1 inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b][color=warrior]Keep Abilities on cooldown[/color][/b] - nearly every rotational Fury ability generates rage, though only [spell=184367] spends it, and in large amounts. This makes it very important to ensure that abilities are constantly being used to ensure that [spell=184361] is constantly maintained, even to the point of delaying Rampage in order to use rage more efficiently.[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
[tr]
[td width=7%][icon name=ability_racial_bloodrage size=medium type=round color=c1 inline=true][/icon][/td]
[td][b][color=warrior]Avoid wasting Rage[/color][/b] - unlike most resources, rage starts from zero and decays out of combat. Making efficient use of it, both in combat and by reducing the amount of time spent moving from one combat to another, will help maintain the rotation and eliminate downtime spent waiting for more resources.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/td][/tr][/table][/center]
[hr]
[b]Reading Priority Lists[/b]
Abilities and talents are listed from highest to lowest priority in the Fury Warrior rotation. Every time an ability is cast, begin again at the top of the list and move down until there is something that can be cast, then return to the top once more.
[/box][/wrapper][pad]

sections.heading: Rotation Priority
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Rotation Priority" type=bar][icon name=ability_warrior_challange type=round inline=true size=medium color=c1][/icon] Best Fury Warrior Rotation[/h2]

For all forms of content, Fury follows a priority list of what spells to cast. Below, we break down the main priority lists for Fury Warriors: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and various openers.


[ul][li][b]New in Patch 12.1[/b]: Rend is now applied passively by Whirlwind and Thunder Clap, and [spell=383877] resets now provide a large bonus to Raging Blow.[/li][/ul]

[tabs name="Rotations" uniform=true]

[tab name="Single Target" icon=spell_holy_divinespirit]

sections.heading: Opener
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Opener" type=bar][icon name=ability_warrior_charge type=round inline=true size=medium color=c1][/icon] Best Fury Warrior Opener[/h2]
Differing from many specializations, the Fury opener is virtually identical to its single-target priority, with the main goal of triggering Enrage as soon as possible. While pre-casting [spell=1719] was an important technique in the past, [spell=385059] and new Apex talents make it no longer necessary.

Unless there are upcoming adds or an increased damage phase, [url=item=133300]stat increasing trinkets[/url] and [url=item=212265]combat potions[/url] are best used on the pull aligned with Recklessness/Avatar, heroism, and other cooldowns. In the case of longer fights with two potions, the second should be saved for a following set of adds, increased damage phase, or Execute whenever possible, though take care to use it early enough that combat won't end before those buffs do.

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][icon name=ability_warrior_innerrage color=c1 inline=true size=medium type=round][/icon] Fury Warrior Major Cooldowns[/h2]

[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Recklessness" icon=warrior_talent_icon_innerrage]
Increases rage generation to enable much more regular use of Rampage, further enhanced by the apex talent [spell=1269309]. With its cooldown reduced by [spell=152278] and aligning perfectly with [spell=107574], it should have a fairly high uptime over the course of a dungeon or encounter.
[/tab]

[tab name="Avatar" icon=warrior_talent_icon_avatar]
A basic damage increase, this is a much more important cooldown for Mountain Thane, due to the influence of [spell=275336], [spell=437134], and [spell=1270724]. It should align perfectly with Recklessness and may therefore be macroed together, though Slayer will instead talent into Bladestorm.
[/tab]

[tab name="Bladestorm" icon=ability_warrior_bladestorm]
A secondary cooldown used exclusively by Slayer, it deals a good amount of single and multitarget damage, while also triggering supplementary effects such as [spell=1270717] and [spell=386628]. It has a unique form of cooldown reduction, so it will not always align with other cooldowns, making it important to think about when to use the cooldown and when to save it.
[/tab]

[tab name="Odyn's Fury" icon=inv_sword_1h_artifactvigfus_d_01]
A talented AoE attack dealing a good amount of single and multitarget damage, it also automatically triggers enrage, making it a good initiator.
[/tab]

[tab name="Champion's Spear" icon=inv_ability_warrior_championsspear]
A talented attack in the class tree, which serves more of a utility role in keeping enemies within an area, though its damage is rather mediocre. The ability can be reactivated to leap to the spear, though this has very niche applications.
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=warrior][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c1][/icon] Fury Warrior Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]

[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Maximizing Uptime"]
Fury Warriors are very straightforward damage dealers, with a very flat damage profile not concentrated entirely into cooldown windows. Because of this, the biggest optimization is simply maximizing uptime on the target - knowing what mechanics are coming [i]before[/i] they actually happen will help plan movement to minimize time spent off target, allowing more rage to be generated and more GCDs to be fit into the overall rotation.

There are a variety of tools to help with this, from using [spell=6544] to move out of range at the last moment before damage goes out, to using [spell=100] after a target has finished moving, which are largely a byproduct of time and experience.
[/tab]
[tab name="Aligning Cooldowns"]
Fury Warriors have several cooldowns, but they're all used more or less the same way - on cooldown as much as possible. When situations or timers allow, cooldowns can be aligned, but they should not be delayed by a significant amount (typically no less than 10-15% of their actual cooldown) unless the delay will allow them to hit multiple targets when they would otherwise hit one, or it will be your final use of the cooldown before the end of the fight regardless.

The reason is that losing an entire use of a cooldown is typically a bigger loss than what is gained by stacking the cooldown with something else to amplify it. Some cooldowns, like [spell=1719] and [spell=107574] will always align naturally, though others will not, so anticipating those timers and knowing when adds or important damage phases are coming is key.
[/tab]
[/tabs]
